objects.description: Configuration structure for creating or preparing an XS virtual machine. Holds initial and incremental sizes for memory arenas, stack, keys, parser buffers, and other VM parameters.
Internal exception/longjmp frame used by the XS VM to implement try/catch and host entry/exit. Links as a stack via nextJump and captures machine execution state.
The XS virtual machine instance. Holds stacks, code pointer, prototypes, host context, archive, and exception linkage. Many APIs take xsMachine* as the execution context.
Generic value container (slot) used by the XS VM to represent JavaScript values and internal references on stacks, frames, and objects.
Descriptor used to build multiple host functions/constructors. Specifies the C callback, argument length, and identifier to define.
Lifecycle hooks for host objects: optional destructor, GC marker, and a signature string used to validate associations.
Enumeration storage type for XS value kinds (e.g., xsUndefinedType, xsNullType, ...). The enum constants are defined in this header; xsType is the underlying char type.
Boolean value representation used by the XS API; underlying signed 32-bit integer.
Integer value representation for the XS API; underlying signed 32-bit integer.
Number (floating-point) representation for the XS API; C double.
Pointer to a C string used by the XS API for UTF-8 strings.
Unsigned 32-bit numeric type used for counts/flags in the XS API.
Signed 8-bit type used by the XS VM for bytecode and other byte-level data.
Small unsigned flag type for bitfields and attributes.
Identifier/index type for property and name IDs. Width depends on configuration (16-bit default or 32-bit if mx32bitID).
Unsigned index type used for array indices and counts.
Function pointer type for host functions and constructors called by the XS VM.
Function pointer type invoked when a host object is finalized; receives host data pointer.
GC helper callback used to mark root slots during collection.
GC mark callback for host data; should mark any referenced slots via the provided xsMarkRoot.
GC sweep callback for root slots. Declared but not used in struct here.
GC sweep callback for host data. Declared but not used in struct here.
Bitfield type for property attributes (xsDontDelete, xsDontEnum, xsDontSet, xsStatic, xsIsGetter, xsIsSetter).
Function pointer returning an xsCallback for a given index. Useful for dispatch tables.

functions.name: fxTypeOf
functions.description: Returns the ECMAScript-like type tag (xsType) of the value stored in the given slot.
requirements: the must be a valid pointer to an initialized xsMachine
slot must point to a valid xsSlot belonging to the same xsMachine

functions.name: fxIsCallable
functions.description: Determines whether the value in slot is callable (i.e., a function). Returns non-zero if callable.
requirements: the must be a valid pointer to an initialized xsMachine
slot must be a valid xsSlot from the same machine

functions.name: fxUndefined
functions.description: Stores the JavaScript undefined value into slot.
requirements: slot must be a valid xsSlot pointer

functions.name: fxNull
functions.description: Stores the JavaScript null value into slot.
requirements: slot must be a valid xsSlot pointer

functions.name: fxBoolean
functions.signature: void fxBoolean(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsBooleanValue value)
functions.description: Stores a Boolean value into slot.
requirements: value is treated as boolean (0 = false, non-zero = true)

functions.name: fxToBoolean
functions.description: Converts the value in slot to boolean and returns it.
requirements: slot must be valid and contain a convertible value

functions.name: fxInteger
functions.signature: void fxInteger(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsIntegerValue value)
functions.description: Stores a 32-bit integer value into slot.

functions.name: fxToInteger
functions.description: Converts the value in slot to a 32-bit integer and returns it.
requirements: slot must be valid and contain a convertible value

functions.name: fxNumber
functions.signature: void fxNumber(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsNumberValue value)
functions.description: Stores a double-precision number into slot.

functions.name: fxToNumber
functions.description: Converts the value in slot to a double-precision number and returns it.
requirements: slot must be valid and contain a convertible value

functions.name: fxString
functions.signature: void fxString(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsStringValue value)
functions.description: Stores a string (C UTF-8) into slot. The engine copies or wraps the provided C string.
requirements: value must be a valid null-terminated UTF-8 string pointer or NULL (behavior for NULL is implementation-defined/unknown)

functions.name: fxStringBuffer
functions.signature: void fxStringBuffer(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsStringValue buffer, xsIntegerValue size)
functions.description: Stores a string into slot using a buffer with explicit byte size (may include embedded zeros).
requirements: buffer points to at least size bytes if size > 0

functions.name: fxStringX
functions.signature: void fxStringX(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsStringValue value)
functions.description: Stores a string into slot without additional safety conversions (eXpert/extended variant). Intended for internal use where string is already valid.
requirements: value must be a valid UTF-8 string pointer

functions.name: fxToString
functions.description: Converts the value in slot to a UTF-8 C string and returns a pointer managed by the engine.
requirements: slot must be valid and convertible to string
Returned pointer is managed by the VM; lifetime/ownership handled by engine (do not free)

functions.name: fxToStringBuffer
functions.signature: xsStringValue fxToStringBuffer(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsStringValue buffer, xsIntegerValue size)
functions.description: Converts slot to string and writes into caller-provided buffer up to size bytes; returns buffer pointer.
requirements: slot must be valid and convertible to string
buffer must point to at least size bytes if size > 0

functions.name: fxToStringX
functions.description: Internal/extended variant to obtain a string pointer from slot; details are engine-specific.
requirements: slot must be valid and convertible to string

functions.name: fxUnsigned
functions.signature: void fxUnsigned(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsUnsignedValue value)
functions.description: Stores an unsigned 32-bit number into slot.

functions.name: fxToUnsigned
functions.description: Converts the value in slot to an unsigned 32-bit number and returns it.
requirements: slot must be valid and contain a convertible value

functions.name: fxFromBigInt64
functions.signature: void fxFromBigInt64(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, int64_t value)
functions.description: Stores a BigInt value (signed 64-bit) into slot.

functions.name: fxToBigInt64
functions.description: Converts the value in slot to a signed 64-bit BigInt and returns it.
requirements: slot must be valid and convertible to BigInt

functions.name: fxFromBigUint64
functions.signature: void fxFromBigUint64(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, uint64_t value)
functions.description: Stores a BigInt value (unsigned 64-bit) into slot.

functions.name: fxToBigUint64
functions.description: Converts the value in slot to an unsigned 64-bit BigInt and returns it.
requirements: slot must be valid and convertible to BigInt

functions.name: fxArrayBuffer
functions.signature: void* fxArrayBuffer(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, void* buffer, xsIntegerValue size, xsIntegerValue maxSize)
functions.description: Creates/assigns an ArrayBuffer into slot. If buffer is non-NULL, its data are used; size defines current length; maxSize >= size enables resizable ArrayBuffer when not -1.
requirements: If buffer is non-NULL, it must point to at least size bytes
If maxSize != -1, it must be >= size

functions.name: fxGetArrayBufferData
functions.signature: void fxGetArrayBufferData(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsIntegerValue offset, void* outBuffer, xsIntegerValue outSize)
functions.description: Copies data from an ArrayBuffer at offset into outBuffer for outSize bytes.
requirements: slot must refer to an ArrayBuffer
offset must be >= 0 and offset + outSize <= buffer length
outBuffer must point to at least outSize bytes when outSize > 0

functions.name: fxGetArrayBufferLength
functions.description: Returns the current byte length of the ArrayBuffer stored in slot.
requirements: slot must refer to an ArrayBuffer

functions.name: fxGetArrayBufferMaxLength
functions.description: Returns the maximum byte length of a resizable ArrayBuffer, or the fixed length for non-resizable buffers.
requirements: slot must refer to an ArrayBuffer

functions.name: fxSetArrayBufferData
functions.signature: void fxSetArrayBufferData(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsIntegerValue offset, void* buffer, xsIntegerValue size)
functions.description: Copies size bytes from buffer into the ArrayBuffer in slot starting at offset.
requirements: slot must refer to an ArrayBuffer
offset >= 0 and offset + size <= current length
buffer must point to at least size bytes if size > 0

functions.name: fxSetArrayBufferLength
functions.signature: void fxSetArrayBufferLength(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsIntegerValue length)
functions.description: Resizes a resizable ArrayBuffer to length bytes, if allowed.
requirements: slot must refer to a resizable ArrayBuffer
length must be >= 0 and <= max length

functions.name: fxToArrayBuffer
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the underlying ArrayBuffer data for the value in slot.
requirements: slot must refer to an ArrayBuffer
Returned pointer is engine-managed; do not free

functions.name: fxClosure
functions.signature: void fxClosure(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsSlot* value)
functions.description: Stores a closure (function environment capture) reference into slot from value.
requirements: slot and value must be valid xsSlot pointers

functions.name: fxToClosure
functions.description: Retrieves the closure reference stored in slot.

functions.name: fxReference
functions.signature: void fxReference(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsSlot* value)
functions.description: Stores a reference to another slot/object into slot.
requirements: slot and value must be valid xsSlot pointers

functions.name: fxToReference
functions.description: Retrieves the referenced slot/object from slot.

functions.name: fxNewArray
functions.description: Allocates a new JavaScript Array with the given length and returns its slot reference (on VM stack in usual macro forms).

functions.name: fxNewObject
functions.description: Allocates a new plain JavaScript object and returns its slot reference.

functions.name: fxIsInstanceOf
functions.description: Performs the JavaScript instanceof check using values on the VM stack (set up by macros). Returns non-zero if true. Low-level API.
requirements: Call only with stack prepared as per xsIsInstanceOf macro usage

functions.name: fxArrayCacheBegin
functions.description: Begins an array element cache session for faster repeated access.
requirements: arraySlot must refer to an Array-like object

functions.name: fxArrayCacheEnd
functions.description: Ends an array element cache session previously started with fxArrayCacheBegin.
requirements: arraySlot must be the same array used with fxArrayCacheBegin

functions.name: fxArrayCacheItem
functions.signature: void fxArrayCacheItem(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* arraySlot, xsSlot* itemSlot)
functions.description: Caches a specific array item for optimized access. Low-level helper used by macros.
requirements: arraySlot and itemSlot must be valid

functions.name: fxBuildHosts
functions.signature: void fxBuildHosts(xsMachine* the, xsIntegerValue count, xsHostBuilder* builders)
functions.description: Creates multiple host functions/constructors from an array of xsHostBuilder records.
requirements: builders must point to at least count entries if count > 0

functions.name: fxNewHostConstructor
functions.signature: xsSlot* fxNewHostConstructor(xsMachine* the, xsCallback callback, xsIntegerValue length, xsIntegerValue id)
functions.description: Creates a new host constructor function with the given callback, length (arity), and optional identifier.
requirements: callback must be a valid function pointer
id may be xsNoID or a valid identifier

functions.name: fxNewHostFunction
functions.signature: xsSlot* fxNewHostFunction(xsMachine* the, xsCallback callback, xsIntegerValue length, xsIntegerValue name, xsIntegerValue lengthID)
functions.description: Creates a new host function with callback and arity. Additional parameters name and lengthID identify metadata (IDs).

functions.name: fxNewHostInstance
functions.description: Allocates a new host object instance using a prototype previously pushed (via macros). Low-level API.
requirements: Call only with VM stack prepared as per xsNewHostInstance macro usage

functions.name: fxNewHostObject
functions.description: Creates a new host object with an optional finalizer (destructor).
requirements: destructor may be NULL or a valid function

functions.name: fxGetHostBufferLength
functions.description: Returns the length (in bytes) of an internal host buffer stored in a host object.
requirements: slot must refer to a host object with buffer

functions.name: fxGetHostChunk
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the host 'chunk' data associated with the object in slot, or NULL if none.
requirements: slot should refer to a host object

functions.name: fxGetHostChunkIf
functions.description: Returns the host chunk pointer if present; otherwise NULL. Variant that does not fault if absent.
requirements: slot should refer to a host object

functions.name: fxGetHostChunkValidate
functions.signature: void* fxGetHostChunkValidate(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, void* validator)
functions.description: Returns the host chunk pointer if the chunk matches/validates against the provided validator (signature).
requirements: slot should refer to a host object
validator must be the expected validation token/signature for the data

functions.name: fxSetHostChunk
functions.signature: void* fxSetHostChunk(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, void* data, xsIntegerValue size)
functions.description: Associates raw data (chunk) of size bytes with the host object in slot and returns the stored pointer (engine-managed).
requirements: slot must refer to a host object
data must point to at least size bytes if size > 0

functions.name: fxGetHostData
functions.description: Returns the host data pointer associated with the object in slot (the generic host data).
requirements: slot should refer to a host object

functions.name: fxGetHostDataIf
functions.description: Returns the host data pointer if present; otherwise NULL. Non-throwing variant.
requirements: slot should refer to a host object

functions.name: fxGetHostDataValidate
functions.signature: void* fxGetHostDataValidate(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, void* validator)
functions.description: Returns the host data pointer if it validates against the supplied validator/signature.
requirements: slot should refer to a host object
validator must match the expected signature for the data

functions.name: fxGetHostDestructor
functions.description: Returns the destructor (finalizer) associated with a host object, or NULL if none.
requirements: slot must refer to a host object

functions.name: fxGetHostHandle
functions.description: Returns the native handle/opaque pointer associated with a host object, if any.
requirements: slot should refer to a host object

functions.name: fxGetHostHooks
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the host hooks (destructor, marker, signature) of a host object. May throw if not present.
requirements: slot must refer to a host object

functions.name: fxGetHostHooksIf
functions.description: Returns the host hooks if present; otherwise NULL. Non-throwing variant.
requirements: slot should refer to a host object

functions.name: fxGetHostHooksValidate
functions.signature: xsHostHooks* fxGetHostHooksValidate(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsStringValue signature)
functions.description: Returns host hooks only if the signature matches the expected string.
requirements: slot should refer to a host object
signature must be a valid C string identifying the expected hooks

functions.name: fxPetrifyHostBuffer
functions.description: Marks the host buffer associated with slot as immutable/non-resizable (petrified).
requirements: slot must refer to a host object with buffer

functions.name: fxSetHostBuffer
functions.signature: void fxSetHostBuffer(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, void* data, xsIntegerValue size)
functions.description: Associates a buffer of size bytes with a host object in slot.
requirements: slot must refer to a host object
data must point to at least size bytes if size > 0

functions.name: fxSetHostData
functions.signature: void fxSetHostData(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, void* data)
functions.description: Stores a native data pointer (host data) into the host object in slot.
requirements: slot must refer to a host object

functions.name: fxSetHostDestructor
functions.signature: void fxSetHostDestructor(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, xsDestructor destructor)
functions.description: Sets the destructor callback for the host object in slot.
requirements: slot must refer to a host object
destructor may be NULL or a valid function

functions.name: fxSetHostHooks
functions.signature: void fxSetHostHooks(xsMachine* the, xsSlot* slot, const xsHostHooks* hooks)
functions.description: Associates host hooks (destructor, marker, signature) with a host object.
requirements: slot must refer to a host object
hooks must be a valid pointer to an xsHostHooks struct

functions.name: fxID
functions.signature: xsIdentifier fxID(xsMachine* the, const char* name)
functions.description: Returns the identifier (atom) for a property name, creating it if necessary.
requirements: name must be a valid C string

functions.name: fxFindID
functions.description: Finds an existing identifier for name if present; may return 0 (XS_NO_ID) if not found.
requirements: name must be a valid C string

functions.name: fxIsID
functions.description: Returns non-zero if name corresponds to a known identifier.
requirements: name must be a valid C string

functions.name: fxToID
functions.description: Converts a value to an identifier (e.g., property key).
requirements: slot must be valid and convertible to an identifier

functions.name: fxName
functions.description: Returns the C string name for an identifier. The returned pointer is engine-managed.
requirements: id must be a valid identifier or XS_NO_ID
Do not free the returned pointer

functions.name: fxEnumerate
functions.description: Prepares an enumeration of properties of the object on the VM stack (used via xsEnumerate macro).
requirements: Call with stack prepared by xsEnumerate macro

functions.name: fxGetAt
functions.description: Retrieves a property by key provided on the VM stack (low-level). Pushes result.
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsGetAt macro (object and key pushed)

functions.name: fxGetID
functions.description: Retrieves a property by identifier from the object on the VM stack and pushes result.
requirements: Object must be on stack per xsGet macro usage
id must be a valid identifier

functions.name: fxGetIndex
functions.description: Retrieves an indexed property from the object on the VM stack and pushes result.
requirements: Object must be on stack per xsGetIndex macro usage

functions.name: fxHasAt
functions.description: Checks if an object has a property for the key provided on the VM stack. Returns non-zero if present.
requirements: Stack must be prepared with object and key as per xsHasAt macro

functions.name: fxHasID
functions.description: Checks if an object on the VM stack has the property with the given identifier.
requirements: Object must be on stack as per xsHas macro

functions.name: fxHasIndex
functions.description: Checks if an object on the VM stack has an indexed property.
requirements: Object must be on stack as per xsHasIndex macro

functions.name: fxSetAt
functions.description: Sets a property by key using object, key, and value on the VM stack. Low-level.
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsSetAt macro with value, object, key

functions.name: fxSetID
functions.description: Sets a property by identifier on the object on the VM stack using the value on the stack.
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsSet macro (value then object)

functions.name: fxSetIndex
functions.description: Sets an indexed property on the object on the VM stack using the value on the stack.
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsSetIndex macro
index must be within representable range

functions.name: fxDefineAt
functions.signature: void fxDefineAt(xsMachine* the, xsAttribute atts, xsAttribute mask)
functions.description: Defines a property by key with specific attributes using items on the VM stack (value, object, key).
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsDefineAt macro
atts and mask are attribute bitfields

functions.name: fxDefineID
functions.signature: void fxDefineID(xsMachine* the, xsIdentifier id, xsAttribute atts, xsAttribute mask)
functions.description: Defines a property by identifier with specific attributes on the object on the VM stack.
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsDefine macro

functions.name: fxDeleteAt
functions.description: Deletes a property by key using object and key on the VM stack.
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsDeleteAt macro

functions.name: fxDeleteID
functions.description: Deletes a property by identifier from the object on the VM stack.
requirements: Object must be on stack (xsDelete macro pattern)

functions.name: fxCall
functions.description: Calls a function using function and this/value on the VM stack per calling macros. Pushes result.
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsCallFunctionN/xsCallN macros

functions.name: fxCallID
functions.description: Calls a method by identifier on an object on the VM stack. Arguments are subsequently pushed and executed via fxRunCount.
requirements: Object must be on stack (xsCallN macros)

functions.name: fxNew
functions.description: Invokes a function as a constructor using items on the VM stack (function and arguments) and pushes the new instance.
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsNewFunctionN macros

functions.name: fxNewID
functions.description: Allocates a new instance by invoking a constructor looked up by id on an object on the VM stack.
requirements: Object must be on stack (xsNewN macros)

functions.name: fxRunCount
functions.description: Runs a prepared call/new with count arguments collected on the VM stack. Produces a result on the stack.
requirements: Must be preceded by a matching fxCall/fxCallID/fxNew/fxNewID

functions.name: fxRunTest
functions.description: Runs a test on the value on the VM stack (used by xsTest macro) to get truthiness. Returns non-zero if truthy.
requirements: Stack must be prepared by xsTest macro

functions.name: fxVars
functions.description: Allocates space for local variables in the current scope/frame (sets xsVarc).

functions.name: fxCheckArg
functions.description: Bounds-checks an argument index and returns a validated index/offset for accessing xsArg(index).

functions.name: fxCheckVar
functions.description: Bounds-checks a local variable index and returns a validated index/offset for accessing xsVar(index).

functions.name: fxOverflow
functions.signature: void fxOverflow(xsMachine* the, xsIntegerValue count, xsStringValue file, xsIntegerValue line)
functions.description: Performs bounds checking on the VM stack to detect over/underflow. In debug builds, file/line identify the caller; otherwise may be NULL/0.
requirements: count indicates required stack space adjustment

functions.name: fxThrow
functions.signature: void fxThrow(xsMachine* the, xsStringValue file, xsIntegerValue line)
functions.description: Throws the current exception stored in xsException and performs non-local exit. Does not return.
requirements: file may be NULL in non-debug builds; line may be 0

functions.name: fxThrowMessage
functions.signature: void fxThrowMessage(xsMachine* the, xsStringValue thePath, xsIntegerValue theLine, xsIntegerValue theError, xsStringValue theMessage, ...)
functions.description: Formats and throws a new exception of the given error class with a formatted message. Does not return.
requirements: theMessage must be a printf-style format string compatible with the variadic arguments
theError must be one of XS_*_ERROR codes

functions.name: fxBubble
functions.signature: void fxBubble(xsMachine* the, xsIntegerValue align, void* data, xsIntegerValue length, xsStringValue id)
functions.description: Sends a formatted trace/log payload to the debugger or output with alignment/direction flags (center/left/right) and optional id.
requirements: data must point to length bytes when length > 0

functions.name: fxDebugger
functions.signature: void fxDebugger(xsMachine* the, xsStringValue file, xsIntegerValue line)
functions.description: Triggers a debugger break/interaction point. In debug builds includes file/line; in release, parameters may be NULL/0.

functions.name: fxReport
functions.description: Formatted logging/trace output using printf-style format string.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string matching variadic arguments

functions.name: fxCreateMachine
functions.signature: xsMachine* fxCreateMachine(xsCreation* creation, xsStringValue name, void* context, xsIdentifier id)
functions.description: Creates and initializes a new xsMachine (virtual machine) with the given creation parameters, optional name/context, and identifier.
requirements: creation must point to a valid xsCreation struct (fields define sizes/counts)
name may be NULL or a C string
context may be any user pointer
id may be xsNoID or a valid identifier

functions.name: fxDeleteMachine
functions.description: Destroys an xsMachine and releases associated resources.
requirements: the must be a machine created by fxCreateMachine/fxPrepareMachine/fxCloneMachine
Must not be used after deletion

functions.name: fxCloneMachine
functions.signature: xsMachine* fxCloneMachine(xsCreation* creation, xsMachine* from, xsStringValue name, void* context)
functions.description: Clones an existing machine's state into a new machine with specified creation parameters and optional name/context.
requirements: from must be a valid, initialized xsMachine

functions.name: fxPrepareMachine
functions.signature: xsMachine* fxPrepareMachine(xsCreation* creation, void* preparation, xsStringValue name, void* context, void* archive)
functions.description: Creates a machine from a preparation (precompiled image) with given creation parameters, optional name/context, and archive pointer.
requirements: preparation must point to a valid preparation blob
archive may be NULL or valid

functions.name: fxShareMachine
functions.description: Marks a machine's state as shared/available to be shared across contexts (details engine-specific).

functions.name: fxBeginHost
functions.description: Prepares the VM for host interaction (entering a host call), returning the same machine pointer for local use.

functions.name: fxEndHost
functions.description: Ends a host interaction previously started with fxBeginHost.
requirements: Must be called after fxBeginHost on the same thread/context

functions.name: fxCollectGarbage
functions.description: Runs the garbage collector.

functions.name: fxEnableGarbageCollection
functions.description: Enables or disables the garbage collector.

functions.name: fxDuplicateSlot
functions.description: Creates a duplicate/copy of the provided slot value and returns a new slot pointer.

functions.name: fxNewChunk
functions.description: Allocates a new memory chunk managed by the VM and returns a pointer.

functions.name: fxRenewChunk
functions.signature: void* fxRenewChunk(xsMachine* the, void* data, xsIntegerValue size)
functions.description: Resizes or reallocates a previously allocated VM-managed chunk to size bytes and returns pointer.
requirements: data must be a pointer previously returned by VM allocation or NULL

functions.name: fxRemember
functions.description: Pins or remembers a slot to prevent it from being collected (adds as GC root).

functions.name: fxForget
functions.description: Removes a previously remembered slot from GC roots.
requirements: slot must be valid and previously passed to fxRemember

functions.name: fxAccess
functions.description: Access barrier/hook for GC to mark a slot’s usage (write/read barrier).

functions.name: fxDecodeURI
functions.description: Decodes a percent-encoded URI component in place or into an engine-managed string (engine-specific).
requirements: string must be a valid C string

functions.name: fxEncodeURI
functions.description: Encodes a URI component (percent-encodes) and stores/manages result.
requirements: string must be a valid C string

functions.name: fxUTF8Decode
functions.description: Decodes a single UTF-8 code point from string, storing the Unicode scalar in character, and returns pointer to next byte.
requirements: string must point to a valid UTF-8 sequence
character must be a valid pointer

functions.name: fxUTF8Encode
functions.description: Encodes a Unicode scalar value into UTF-8 at string and returns pointer advanced past the encoded bytes.
requirements: string must point to sufficient space to hold the encoded character (up to 4 bytes)
character must be a valid Unicode scalar (0..0x10FFFF)

functions.name: fxUTF8Length
functions.description: Returns the number of UTF-8 bytes needed to encode the given Unicode scalar.
requirements: character must be a valid Unicode scalar (0..0x10FFFF)

functions.name: fxUTF8ToUnicodeOffset
functions.description: Converts a byte offset in a UTF-8 string to a Unicode code point index.
requirements: theString must be a valid UTF-8 string
theOffset must be >= 0 and within the byte length

functions.name: fxUnicodeLength
functions.description: Returns the number of Unicode code points in a UTF-8 string and optionally writes the total byte length to byteLength.
requirements: theString must be a valid UTF-8 string
byteLength may be NULL or a valid pointer

functions.name: fxUnicodeToUTF8Offset
functions.description: Converts a Unicode code point index to the corresponding UTF-8 byte offset.
requirements: theString must be a valid UTF-8 string
theOffset must be >= 0 and <= number of code points

functions.name: fxIntegerToString
functions.signature: xsStringValue fxIntegerToString(xsMachine* the, xsIntegerValue value, xsStringValue buffer, xsIntegerValue size)
functions.description: Formats an integer into buffer as a C string and returns buffer.
requirements: buffer must point to at least size bytes if size > 0

functions.name: fxNumberToString
functions.signature: xsStringValue fxNumberToString(xsMachine* the, xsNumberValue value, xsStringValue buffer, xsIntegerValue size, char theMode, xsIntegerValue thePrecision)
functions.description: Formats a number into buffer according to mode/precision and returns buffer.
requirements: buffer must have at least size bytes if size > 0
theMode and thePrecision semantics are engine-defined

functions.name: fxStringToNumber
functions.signature: xsNumberValue fxStringToNumber(xsMachine* the, xsStringValue theString, unsigned char whole)
functions.description: Parses a C string as a number and returns the numeric value. whole indicates integer-only mode when non-zero.
requirements: theString must be a valid C string

functions.name: fxDemarshall

data_types.description: A null-terminated C string containing UTF-8 encoded text. May be empty. Must not contain embedded nulls except for the terminator. Suitable for APIs expecting const char* C strings.

A byte buffer treated as raw bytes with an explicit length. May contain any byte values including embedded nulls. Used when APIs take a pointer and a size to construct or process data that need not be valid text.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for UTF-8 C strings intended for FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls across stubs.
# Goals:
# - Produce valid, null-terminated UTF-8 (no embedded NULs, terminator added by fuzzer harness if needed).
# - Cover interesting inputs for identifiers, URIs, regex, numbers, names, and general strings.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded randomness.
# - Return bytes that the harness will consume sequentially for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and other scalar params.
#
# Assumptions:
# - The harness reads from the provided buffer to fulfill FUZZ_PARAM_STR and numeric FUZZ_PARAM<T>.
# - We therefore interleave a small header describing how many strings and their lengths/content so the
#   harness can slice deterministically. Many fuzzers just read bytes sequentially; to make it robust,
#   we emit a sequence of N strings concatenated with length prefixes. Since the stubs only use STRs
#   (no FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME), emitting diverse strings in sequence is beneficial.
# - Numeric FUZZ_PARAMs are handled by the fuzzer; we simply ensure enough trailing random bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Some useful string families to exercise the targets
ASCII_WORDS = [
    "id", "name", "length", "toString", "value", "constructor", "prototype",
    "get", "set", "has", "delete", "match", "encode", "decode",
]
NUMERIC_LIKE = [
    "0", "1", "-1", "42", "-9007199254740991", "9007199254740991", "3.14159",
    "1e10", "-2.5e-3", "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity",
]
URIS = [
    "", "/", "./a", "../b", "http://example.com/", "https://example.com?q=1",
    "file:///etc/hosts", "%20space%2Fslash", "a%F0%9F%92%A9b",  # includes valid percent and emoji
]
REGEX_PATTERNS = [
    ".*", "^$", "[a-z]+", "(foo|bar)?", "^\d{1,3}(?:\.\d{1,3}){3}$", "^hello$",
    "[😀-🙏]",  # unicode class via explicit range of emoji (UTF-8)
]
REGEX_FLAGS = ["", "i", "g", "m", "u", "imu", "sy"]
IDENTIFIERS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "δelta", "π", "Ωmega", "ключ", "名前", "اسم", "παράδειγμα",
]
DEBUG_FILENAMES = [
    "main.c", "vm.cpp", "engine.c", "module.js", "path/with spaces/file.txt",
]

# Some helper to build random UTF-8 including multi-byte code points
BMP_BLOCKS = [
    (0x0020, 0x007E),  # printable ASCII
    (0x00A1, 0x024F),  # Latin-1 Supplement, Latin Extended
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),  # Greek
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),  # Cyrillic
    (0x0590, 0x05FF),  # Hebrew
    (0x0600, 0x06FF),  # Arabic
    (0x3040, 0x30FF),  # Hiragana/Katakana
    (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),  # CJK Unified Ideographs (subset)
]
EMOJI_RANGE = (0x1F300, 0x1F64F)

def rand_code_point(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        # include some emoji/supplementary
        return rng.randint(*EMOJI_RANGE)
    lo, hi = rng.choice(BMP_BLOCKS)
    return rng.randint(lo, hi)

def encode_utf8(cp: int) -> str:
    # return as Python str (which is Unicode); Python will handle UTF-8 encoding at the end
    return chr(cp)

def rand_utf8_string(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = []
    for _ in range(length):
        cp = rand_code_point(rng)
        # avoid embedded NULs in C string
        if cp == 0:
            cp = 0x20
        s.append(encode_utf8(cp))
    return "".join(s)

def weighted_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str], weight: float = 0.5, fallback_gen=None) -> str:
    if items and rng.random() < weight:
        return rng.choice(items)
    return fallback_gen() if fallback_gen else ""

def build_string_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool: List[str] = []

    # Important themed strings to hit various APIs
    pool.extend(ASCII_WORDS)
    pool.extend(IDENTIFIERS)
    pool.extend(NUMERIC_LIKE)
    pool.extend(URIS)
    pool.extend(REGEX_PATTERNS)
    pool.extend(REGEX_FLAGS)
    pool.extend(DEBUG_FILENAMES)

    # Add several random UTF-8 strings of varying lengths
    for _ in range(10):
        pool.append(rand_utf8_string(rng, 0, 24))
    for _ in range(5):
        pool.append(rand_utf8_string(rng, 25, 80))

    # Strings tailored for property keys and IDs
    for _ in range(6):
        base = weighted_choice(rng, IDENTIFIERS, 0.7, lambda: rand_utf8_string(rng, 3, 12))
        # sometimes add dots/colons to exercise different key shapes
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            base = base + ("." + weighted_choice(rng, ASCII_WORDS, 0.7, lambda: rand_utf8_string(rng, 2, 6)))
        pool.append(base)

    # Patterns for regex compile
    for _ in range(6):
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            pool.append(weighted_choice(rng, REGEX_PATTERNS, 0.8, lambda: rand_utf8_string(rng, 1, 10)))
        else:
            # realistic email-ish or ip-ish
            user = rand_utf8_string(rng, 3, 8)
            host = rand_utf8_string(rng, 3, 8)
            pool.append(f"{user}@{host}.com")

    # For URI encode/decode
    for _ in range(6):
        base = rand_utf8_string(rng, 0, 20)
        # sprinkle reserved characters
        reserved = ":/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;="
        for _i in range(rng.randint(0, 5)):
            pos = rng.randint(0, len(base))
            base = base[:pos] + rng.choice(reserved) + base[pos:]
        pool.append(base)

    # For fxReport/fxDebugger names/ids
    for _ in range(4):
        pool.append("log_" + rand_utf8_string(rng, 3, 12))

    # Ensure empty string present
    pool.append("")

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for s in pool:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)
    return uniq

def pack_len_prefixed_strings(strings: List[str], budget: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # We pack as: [count:2 bytes][len:2][bytes][len:2][bytes]...
    # This format is generic; the fuzzer harness may ignore lengths, but concatenation ensures availability.
    # Limit total <= budget.
    out = bytearray()
    # Reserve space for count; fill later
    out.extend(b"\x00\x00")
    count = 0
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8')  # valid UTF-8
        if b"\x00" in b:
            # extremely rare as we avoid cp=0, but check anyway
            b = b.replace(b"\x00", b" ")
        # ensure space for len + data
        if len(out) + 2 + len(b) > budget:
            break
        out.extend(len(b).to_bytes(2, 'little'))
        out.extend(b)
        count += 1
    # write count at start
    out[0:2] = count.to_bytes(2, 'little')
    return bytes(out)

def pad_random_tail(buf: bytes, budget: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    remaining = budget - len(buf)
    if remaining <= 0:
        return buf
    # Add some random bytes to satisfy non-string FUZZ_PARAM reads
    tail = bytearray(remaining)
    for i in range(remaining):
        tail[i] = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    return buf + bytes(tail)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a diverse pool and shuffle slightly based on seed
    pool = build_string_pool(rng)
    rng.shuffle(pool)

    # Ensure we front-load certain categories to align with early STR uses:
    front = []
    # identifiers first
    front.append(weighted_choice(rng, IDENTIFIERS, 1.0, lambda: "key"))
    # a regex pattern and flags
    front.append(weighted_choice(rng, REGEX_PATTERNS, 1.0, lambda: ".*"))
    front.append(weighted_choice(rng, REGEX_FLAGS, 1.0, lambda: ""))
    # a URI-like string
    front.append(weighted_choice(rng, URIS, 1.0, lambda: "/"))
    # a numeric-like string
    front.append(weighted_choice(rng, NUMERIC_LIKE, 1.0, lambda: "42"))
    # a general UTF-8 random string
    front.append(rand_utf8_string(rng, 5, 20))

    # Merge front with remainder, keeping uniqueness
    used = set(front)
    rest = [s for s in pool if s not in used]
    strings = front + rest

    # Pack within budget and add random tail
    body = pack_len_prefixed_strings(strings, min(MAX_TOTAL, 3500), rng)
    final = pad_random_tail(body, MAX_TOTAL, rng)
    return final

import random
import struct
import string

# Generator for arbitrary binary data intended for fxStringBuffer(the, slot, buffer, size)
# The fuzzer uses:
#   std::string src = FUZZ_PARAM_STR();
#   xsIntegerValue size = src.empty() ? 0 : rand % min(src.size(), 256)
#   fxStringBuffer(..., src.data(), size)
# So we want to produce a bytes buffer that, when treated as a C++ std::string payload, provides
# interesting binary content with a variety of lengths and embedded NULs, and reasonably sized
# (<= 4096 bytes total). The fuzzer will pick a size up to 255 (or src length), so ensure
# we often provide src length >= 256 to allow full 0..255 sizes and also smaller lengths.

ASCII_WORDS = [
    b"", b"A", b"abc", b"hello", b"world", b"Moddable", b"XS", b"ArrayBuffer",
    b"\x00", b"\x00\x00", b"null", b"undefined", b"true", b"false",
]

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "ñ", "é", "漢字", "🙂", "€", "Ω", "𐍈", "𝄞", "🏳️\u200d🌈", "💯",
]

BASE_TOKENS = [
    b"0", b"1", b"-1", b"42", b"3.14159", b"NaN", b"Infinity", b"-Infinity",
    b"0xFF", b"1e309", b"-0",
]

CONTROL_SEQUENCES = [
    b"\x00", b"\x01", b"\x02", b"\x03", b"\x7F", b"\x80", b"\xFF",
]

HEX_BYTES = bytes(range(256))

def _rand_utf8_chunks(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix valid UTF-8 and binary to test both text-like and arbitrary bytes.
    parts = []
    while sum(len(p) for p in parts) < target_len:
        choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            parts.append(rng.choice(ASCII_WORDS))
        elif choice == 1:
            # Add a random unicode string encoded as UTF-8
            s = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
            # Repeat occasionally
            s *= rng.randint(1, 3)
            parts.append(s.encode('utf-8'))
        elif choice == 2:
            # Random alphanum run
            run = rng.randint(1, 32)
            parts.append(''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(run)).encode('ascii'))
        elif choice == 3:
            # Some numbers and keywords
            parts.append(rng.choice(BASE_TOKENS))
        else:
            # Control / high bytes
            run = rng.randint(1, 16)
            start = rng.randint(0, 255 - run)
            parts.append(HEX_BYTES[start:start+run])
        # Occasionally insert NULs inside
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append(b"\x00" * rng.randint(1, 4))
        # Occasionally insert very high bytes
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            parts.append(bytes([rng.randint(128, 255) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))]))
    data = b"".join(parts)
    if len(data) > target_len:
        data = data[:target_len]
    return data

def _structured_prefixes(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Create structured headers that might trigger different paths in string handling
    prefixes = []
    # Length-prefixed block (not required by API, but good binary variety)
    block_len = rng.randint(0, 64)
    prefixes.append(struct.pack('<I', block_len))
    prefixes.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(block_len)))
    # Repeated pattern block
    patt = bytes([rng.randint(0, 255)]) * rng.randint(1, 32)
    repeat = rng.randint(1, 16)
    prefixes.append(patt * repeat)
    # Insert separators and NULs
    prefixes.append(b"\x00\x00")
    # Some common substrings
    for token in [b"/", b"\\", b"::", b"\n", b"\r\n", b",", b";", b"="]:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            prefixes.append(token)
    return b"".join(prefixes)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide an overall target size for src (the fuzzer will choose size <= min(len(src), 256))
    # Bias toward >= 256 to allow full range, but sometimes smaller and sometimes very small/empty.
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.1:
        total_len = 0  # empty string case
    elif roll < 0.25:
        total_len = rng.randint(1, 64)  # small
    elif roll < 0.8:
        total_len = rng.randint(256, 1024)  # typical large enough for 0..255 sizes
    else:
        total_len = rng.randint(65, 255)  # medium below 256

    # Build the payload
    parts = []
    if total_len > 0:
        # Start with some structured prefix to diversify early bytes
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            pref = _structured_prefixes(rng)
            parts.append(pref)
        # Add a UTF-8/binary mix to reach the target length
        remaining = max(0, total_len - sum(len(p) for p in parts))
        parts.append(_rand_utf8_chunks(rng, remaining))
        data = b"".join(parts)
        # Trim or pad to exact length
        if len(data) > total_len:
            data = data[:total_len]
        elif len(data) < total_len:
            # Pad with random bytes including NULs
            pad_len = total_len - len(data)
            pad = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(pad_len))
            data += pad
    else:
        data = b""

    # Ensure final buffer limit
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    return data
